tests: Discovery works on a stack that is not Flutter — the portability proof
query: อยากได้ design system ใน Figma จากโปรเจกต์นี้
files: evals/fixtures/react-mini/ — a Vite + React project, no node_modules, nothing installed
package.json: react, react-router-dom, @storybook/react-vite, @storybook/test-runner, playwright, tailwindcss; packageManager is pnpm
src/styles/tokens.css — CSS custom properties: primitives, semantic aliases of those primitives, one rgba() overlay with alpha, spacing, radius, type
tailwind.config.js — every entry is a var() reference back to tokens.css; nothing is defined there
No shadow custom property anywhere; boxShadow written inline in Button.tsx
src/App.tsx — createBrowserRouter with two routes, one carrying a redirect loader
expected_behavior: Identifies React + Vite from package.json, and pnpm from the packageManager field — not from a lockfile guess

Names tokens.css as the source of truth and tailwind.config.js as a VIEW of it, with the reason: a developer changing a colour edits tokens.css. Extracting from the tailwind config would yield var() references instead of values
Recognises the semantic layer as aliases and says the chain must be resolved before comparing values, or every alias reads as a mismatch
Reports the shadow family as absent with evidence (inline boxShadow in Button.tsx, no custom property), and does not invent shadow tokens
Notes the overlay's alpha must survive extraction and comparison
Detects the existing Storybook and that it can already produce images (test-runner plus playwright are present), so the catalog question is 'reuse' not 'build'
Names src/App.tsx as the flow source, and classifies the redirect loader as a `guard` edge rather than an `action` edge
Raises responsive breakpoints as a decision the human has to make — a web product has no single frame size — rather than silently picking one
Does all of this without running npm install or any build
baseline_failure: Reaches for tailwind.config.js because it is the recognisable 'theme file', and produces a token set of var() strings — or extracts Tailwind's entire default palette as if it were the product's design system. Misses that the semantic layer is aliased, and invents a shadow scale because a design system is expected to have one.
